## Conformance notes

- **curt-openwith** — Docs-reconcile addition 2026-11-01, no code audit run — port claims verified only against the source comments, not vectors or a test suite.
- **curtis** — Fails L1 by the letter: parseCurt has no BOM tolerance. Naming divergent (L2 fail).
- **curtis-ai-chat-porter** — L1 pass-in-practice but fails by the letter (BOM stripped incidentally by TextDecoder, not parseCurt). L2 fail (own sanitizer).
- **curtis-web** — No reader exists; L1 untestable. Write-side conforms (verbatim envelope, generator stamped). L2 fail (title-only filenames).
- **curtis-cloud** — Fails L1: no BOM tolerance, drops top-level envelope extras.
- **curtis-ai-tech** — L1 pass-in-practice via porter-derived path; fails by the letter. L2 fail.
- **tractum** — Not yet run against conformance/ vectors (Python vs TS runner); validate_curt covers L1+L2 envelope+naming rules by construction. Audit pending.
- **curt-vcon** — Not run against conformance/ vectors. All v1 parsing/serialization is the reference implementation's by construction (single dependency, no vendored copy); the bridge's own lossy mapping is covered by 18 tests (pass 2026-11-01).
- **curt-convert** — Not run against conformance/ vectors. As a writer, L1 parse rules apply only via its self-check (parseCurt on every body before it is written). Validated 2026-11-01 against the author's full real-session corpus: 1168/1168 transcripts converted, 0 self-check failures, exit 0. Re-validated 2026-11-01 after the bulk collision fix: 1169/1169 transcripts (corpus grew by one), 1169 distinct output filenames, 0 self-check failures, identical file lists across two runs.
- **curt-wildchat** — Not run against conformance/ vectors. L3-style bulk artifact: CONFORMANCE-1K corpus run — 1000 records → 995 files, 100% independent re-parse, 1.126× envelope overhead. 17 tests pass 2026-11-01.
- **curt-openwebui** — Not run against conformance/ vectors. TS side validated by 15 tests incl. a fixture round-trip through reference parseCurt (pass 2026-11-01). Python side: own validator mirrors the v1 structural rules; cross-validated 2026-11-01 — a pipeline-written .curt body parses valid in the reference JS parseCurt (ad-hoc cross-check, not a vector run). The pipeline itself is draft: never exercised in a live Open WebUI pipelines runtime.

## Ecosystem findings

- ZERO consumers depend on the npm curt-format package — all five implement or vendor their own copy of the rules.
- Only the dot_curt reference implements the 1.1.0 BOM rule; every consumer fails a BOM-prefixed file (porter only by accident of TextDecoder).
- Nobody implements the documented curtFilename naming convention — three different sanitizers, none matching SPEC.md.
- All copies are v1-strict on parse, which is the spec's most load-bearing rule — that part has held.
- Version lineage is broken: porter's oracle pins curtis-ai-chat v2.0.1 (1c7a19f) but that repo now self-identifies as curtis@1.0.0.
- 2026-11-01: the first npm-dependency consumers exist — curt-vcon, curt-convert, and curt-openwebui (TS side) depend on curt-format@1.2.0 instead of vendoring the rules. The zero-dependency finding above still holds for the five original consumers.
- 2026-11-01: all three new consumers are same-author (JordanNewell) local builds — none published to GitHub or npm. Same-author emissions do not promote draft extensions: curt-convert's tool-linkage emission keeps the extension at draft (stable requires two independent implementations).
- 2026-11-01 (publish day, supersedes the previous finding's publication half): curt-vcon@1.0.1, curt-convert@1.0.2, and curt-wildchat@1.0.2 are live on npm; curt-vcon, curt-convert, curt-wildchat, and curt-openwith are public GitHub repos (Gitea-SSOT + GH mirror). curt-openwebui remains local/unpublished. Same-author rule unchanged: draft extensions stay draft.
